2025_091_asbo_award.paragraph: Award packet documenting that the Association of School Business Officials International (ASBO) granted Troy School District its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024. The packet contains the certificate, a June 18, 2025 congratulatory letter to Assistant Superintendent of Business Services Daniel Trudel, an ASBO press release, and the review team's comments dated June 16, 2025. The review team awarded the certificate by consensus and issued a single improvement comment about analysis of individual major capital projects funds.
2025_091_asbo_award.page:
**The award**
ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting is presented to Troy School District for its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024. The certificate states that the district report meets the criteria established for the award and is signed by Ryan S. Stechschulte, President, and James M. Rowan, CAE, SFO, CEO/Executive Director.

**Notification letter**
Dated June 18, 2025 and addressed to Daniel Trudel, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Rd, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777. Signed by James M. Rowan, CEO/Executive Director. The letter encourages use of the COE recipient's logo in emails and marketing materials, and instructs the district to review and address the review team's comments before preparing next year's report; a copy of the original comments and the district's written responses must be included in next year's application packet. A press release and the award certificate were attached.

**Press release**
For immediate release from Reston, VA, dated June 18, 2025; media contact Allison Barton-Kramer, abarton-kramer@asbointl.org. The release quotes Jim Rowan, CAE, SFO, Executive Director: "For over half a century, ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting has been the gold standard for promoting and recognizing excellence in financial transparency." It notes that submitted ACFRs are reviewed by a panel of experienced financial professionals and that the distinction supports bond rating and continuing bond disclosure processes. The program is sponsored by Strategic Partner American Fidelity; more information at asbointl.org/COE. ASBO International was established in 1910 and unites a global network of approximately 30,000 school business professionals.

**Review comments**
Dated June 16, 2025 for Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024. The review team reached consensus to award the Certificate of Excellence, commended the district for its efforts, and described the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report as being of high quality. One comment was issued, referencing page 7: include analysis of significant balances and transactions of the individual major funds (capital projects), citing eGAAFR chapter 31, page 606.

**GASB updates provided as a courtesy**

| Statement | Subject | Issued | Effective for periods beginning after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No. 101 | Compensated Absences | June 2022 | December 15, 2023 |
| No. 102 | Certain Risk Disclosures | December 2023 | June 15, 2024 |
| No. 103 | Financial Reporting Model Improvements | April 2024 | June 15, 2025 |
| No. 104 | Disclosure of Certain Capital Assets | September 2024 | June 15, 2025 |

ASBO International's address on the comment letter is 11160 C-1 South Lakes Drive, #808, Reston, VA 20191, phone 866.682.2729.
2025_091_asbo_award.verbose:
Board packet material presenting Troy School District's receipt of the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting from the Association of School Business Officials International (ASBO), together with the underlying correspondence, press release and review-team comments.

CERTIFICATE. The certificate reads that the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting is presented to Troy School District for its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024, and that the district report meets the criteria established for ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting. It carries the signatures of Ryan S. Stechschulte, President, and James M. Rowan, CAE, SFO, CEO/Executive Director.

NOTIFICATION LETTER. Dated June 18, 2025, the letter is addressed to Daniel Trudel, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Rd, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777, and opens "Dear Daniel." Writing on behalf of ASBO, James M. Rowan informs the district that Troy School District has received ASBO's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, characterizing the award as a significant achievement that reflects the district's commitment to transparency and high-quality financial reporting. The letter encourages the district to use the COE recipient's logo to share the achievement in emails and marketing materials. It states that the Certificate of Excellence (COE) Review Team has provided comments for the improvement of the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, that it is important to review the comments and address them before preparing next year's report, and that the district must include a copy of the original comments and the district's written responses to those comments in next year's application packet. A press release for sharing the achievement with the community and the award certificate were attached. The letter closes with congratulations to Trudel and the staff members who worked to earn the COE and an expression of interest in the district's continued participation in the COE program.

PRESS RELEASE. Marked FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE, with contact Allison Barton-Kramer at abarton-kramer@asbointl.org, and datelined Reston, VA - June 18, 2025. Headlined "Troy School District Honored with ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting," the release announces that Troy School District (Michigan) has been awarded the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting (COE), an honor that recognizes school districts upholding the highest standards of financial reporting and transparency. The district earned the certificate for its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024. Jim Rowan, CAE, SFO, Executive Director of ASBO International, is quoted: "For over half a century, ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting has been the gold standard for promoting and recognizing excellence in financial transparency. Clear and accurate financial reporting is crucial for engaging school communities and building their trust. Districts that earn the COE have demonstrated an extraordinary commitment to these principles." The release explains that participation in the COE program highlights a district's dedication to financial accountability, that submitted ACFRs are rigorously reviewed by a panel of experienced financial professionals who provide constructive feedback to enhance the quality of future reports, and that districts meeting the program's stringent requirements are awarded the Certificate of Excellence - a distinction that also supports bond rating and continuing bond disclosure processes. The program is proudly sponsored by Strategic Partner American Fidelity, and readers are directed to asbointl.org/COE.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATIONS. The release notes that ASBO International was established in 1910 and is a nonprofit organization that unites, through its members and affiliates, a global network of approximately 30,000 school business professionals, empowering members with programs, resources and connections intended to set the standard for excellence in school business management; more information at asbointl.org. A companion section on American Fidelity describes the company as familiar with the education community, functioning as an extension of a district's HR department, administering the entire benefits program, educating employees through in-person education and customized communications, providing an enrollment platform for benefits enrollment, and helping keep the district and its program compliant.

REVIEW COMMENTS. Dated June 16, 2025, the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting Review Comments are addressed to Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024. The document states that it is the consensus of the review team to award the Certificate of Excellence, that the District is to be commended for its efforts, and that the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report is of high quality. Under the FINANCIAL SECTION heading, one comment is listed at reference page 7, item 1: include analysis of significant balances and transactions of the individual major funds (capital projects), with a citation to eGAAFR chapter 31, page 606.

GASB UPDATES. Provided as a courtesy, the review comments list the Governmental Accounting Standards Board statements the district should consider, as applicable, in preparing future Annual Comprehensive Financial Reports. GASB Statement No. 101, Compensated Absences, issued June 2022, updates the recognition and measurement guidance for compensated absences by aligning that guidance under a unified model and amending certain previously required disclosures; its requirements are effective for periods beginning after December 15, 2023. GASB Statement No. 102, Certain Risk Disclosures, issued December 2023, establishes financial reporting requirements for risks related to vulnerabilities due to certain concentrations or constraints; effective for periods beginning after June 15, 2024. GASB Statement No. 103, Financial Reporting Model Improvements, issued April 2024, improves key components of the financial reporting model to enhance its effectiveness in providing information essential for decision-making and assessing a government's accountability, and addresses certain application issues; effective for periods beginning after June 15, 2025. GASB Statement No. 104, Disclosure of Certain Capital Assets, issued September 2024, provides users of financial statements with essential information about certain types of capital assets in order to make informed decisions and assess accountability; effective for periods beginning after June 15, 2025. The comment document carries ASBO International's address, 11160 C-1 South Lakes Drive, #808, Reston, VA 20191, and phone 866.682.2729.

2025_092_8_a_admin.paragraph: Bid award recommendation from Barton Malow Builders for Bid Package #5, the Troy School District Administration Building Renovation, transmitted August 26, 2025 to Assistant Superintendent of Business Services Dan Trudel. Bids were opened publicly on August 12, 2025 and reviewed with project architect TMP Architecture Inc. Eight trade contracts are recommended for a total contractor direct cost of $1,418,803, which with a 10% contingency of $141,880.30 produces a total construction cost of $1,560,683.30. Barton Malow expressly declines to recommend the lowest General Trades and Carpentry bidder, citing recent performance concerns on similar Barton Malow bond programs.

2025_094_2025_annual_leadership_conferen.verbose:
Web page printout of the Michigan Association of School Boards 2025 Annual Leadership Conference overview, retrieved 8/28/25 at 1:19 PM from https://www.masb.org/learning/upcoming-events/annual-leadership-conference/ and reproduced across 12 pages. Breadcrumb: HOME / LEARNING / UPCOMING EVENTS / 2025 ANNUAL LEADERSHIP CONFERENCE.

EVENT DESCRIPTION. The 2025 Annual Leadership Conference carries the theme "Beyond the Horizon - Choose Your Own Adventure" and runs Oct. 23-26, 2025 at the Grand Traverse Resort and Spa in Acme. The page invites attendees to journey beyond the horizon at this year's conference in the Traverse City area, describing ALC as a must-attend event for both new and experienced board members, educators and administrators from across Michigan that brings together the brightest minds in education leadership to collectively shape the future of Michigan's schools. Attendees are told they can choose their own adventure through innovative keynotes, interactive sessions, unique networking activities and transformative learning experiences, with conference tracks designed to build lasting connections and offerings for those seeking certification opportunities, governance insights, or innovative approaches to student achievement. Navigation links include REGISTER NOW, VIEW SCHEDULE and REGISTRATION CHECKLIST, plus a CONTACT US prompt and section anchors for General Sessions, Conference Registration Rates, Schedule At-a-Glance, Add-on Registration Options, Resort Accommodations, General Information, Event Policies, Exhibit Show and For Exhibitors.

GENERAL SESSIONS. "Embracing Innovation to Help Every Learner Find Success in Their Own Way" with George Couros, Leadership Consultant and Author, Friday, Oct. 24. "Leading Through Complexity: Strengthening Trust and Decision-Making" with Matt Lehrman, Social Prosperity Partners, Saturday, Oct. 25. Each carries a LEARN MORE link.

CONFERENCE REGISTRATION RATES. Attendees are urged to register by Aug. 29 and save. Main Conference $440, rising to $465 after Aug. 29, 2025; includes the Thursday Welcome Reception, Friday and Saturday breakfast and lunch, general sessions and clinic sessions. Virtual Conference $249; includes access to the event mobile app and livestreaming of Friday and Saturday general sessions. Friday One-Day Conference $249, rising to $275 after Aug. 29, 2025; includes Friday only breakfast, lunch, general session and clinic sessions. Saturday One-Day Conference $249, rising to $275 after Aug. 29, 2025; includes Saturday only breakfast, lunch, general sessions and clinic sessions.

RESORT ACCOMMODATIONS. The host property is the Grand Traverse Resort and Spa, 100 Grand Traverse Village Blvd, Acme, MI 49610, with a Hotel Guestroom rate of $199 and a Tower Guestroom rate of $259, a reservation deadline of Sept. 24, 2025 or until sold out, and reservations available online or by calling 800.968.7352 and mentioning the Michigan Association of School Boards. Rates are before applicable taxes/fees and daily resort fee, and proof of sales tax exemption must be received by the hotel.

OVERFLOW ACCOMMODATIONS. Alexandria Inn, 3.7 miles from Grand Traverse Resort, 2227 US 31 North, Traverse City, MI 49686: $169 on Wednesday and Thursday, $229 on Friday and Saturday; reservation deadline Sept. 22, 2025 or until sold out; call 231.938.6468 and mention the Michigan Association of School Boards; two-night minimum stay required and proof of sales tax exemption must be received by the hotel by Sept. 22, 2025. Pointes North Beachfront Hotel, 3.8 miles away, 2211 North US 31 North, Traverse City, MI 49686: $99 on Wednesday and Thursday, $159 on Friday and Saturday; deadline Sept. 10, 2025 or until sold out; call 231.938.9191; two-night minimum and proof of sales tax exemption required prior to arrival. Sleep Inn & Suites, 1.8 miles away, 5520 US 31 North, Acme, MI 49610: $89 on Wednesday and Thursday, $159 on Friday and Saturday; deadline Sept. 10, 2025 or until sold out; reservations online or call 231.938.7000; two-night minimum and proof of sales tax exemption required prior to arrival. Holiday Inn Express & Suites, 1.8 miles away, 3536 Mt. Hope Road, Acme, MI 49690: room rate $145; deadline Oct. 1, 2025 or until sold out; reservations online or call 231.938.2600; proof of sales tax exemption must be received by the hotel 30 days prior to arrival. All quoted rates are before applicable taxes and fees.

CONTACTS. Registration and general questions: Katie Kosmider, Membership Coordinator and Registrar. Lodging and accommodations: Whitney Haughey, CMP, Conference and Events Planner. Exhibitor and sponsor questions: Stacy Washington, Marketing Coordinator. Each entry carries a CONTACT ME link.

MASB EDUCATION CREDITS. Education credits are earned by registering and attending; attendance is verified when participants check in and pick up their registration packets on site, or verified via Zoom for virtual attendance. Thursday Delegate Assembly earns 10 credits. Friday and Saturday Main Conference earns 40 credits. Friday or Saturday One-Day Conference earns 20 credits. Virtual general sessions only earns 20 credits. Separately, administrators and educators receive State Continuing Education Clock Hours (SCECH) certification credits for attendance upon approval; required forms will be available at the MASB registration desk or can be submitted online via a BEGIN FORM link.

DELEGATE ASSEMBLY. No cost, pre-registration required for delegates. All delegates and alternates must be school board members, and only delegates and alternates named by a board may offer motions and vote on issues; however, all school board members may speak on the issues and participate in the debate. Thursday, Oct. 23: Delegate Assembly Registration 6-7 p.m., Delegate Assembly 7-8:30 p.m.

SOCIAL AND NETWORKING EVENTS. The Welcome Reception is Thursday, Oct. 23 from 8:30-9:30 p.m., following the conclusion of Delegate Assembly, featuring signature drinks and appetizers. The Exhibit Show is Friday, Oct. 24 from noon-2 p.m., with exclusive hours to network with businesses from across the state that assist schools in areas ranging from accounting and architectural firms to technology and building services. The Sips and S'mores Social Event is Friday, Oct. 24 from 8-9 p.m., offering networking with school board members from across Michigan over s'mores and drinks.
